integrity: The exact finite fidelity and variance identities follow directly from the state amplitudes. The universal limit follows from an explicitly normalized triangular-array central limit theorem and vanishing quadratic remainder. Complete-graph theta asymptotics use a uniform local binomial approximation with tail control. Finite tests are corroborative only.
scientific_limitations: The results concern full-state fidelity under one common centered Gaussian edge-phase miscalibration per preparation, not independent Pauli or independently distributed edge errors. The general Gaussian limit requires the displayed high-degree regularity conditions; star and complete graphs are separate exact examples. No hardware-level or fault-tolerance guarantees are asserted.
title: Degree-norm calibration law and lattice crossover for common-mode graph-state phase noise
